description: HORIZON 89 is a multidisciplinary student team developing an intuitive, scientifically grounded platform for the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge. We aim to simplify lunar south-pole mission planning through interactive 3D visualization of solar illumination, Earth visibility, communication access, and site-specific operational conditions.
summary:
**HORIZON 89 – Beyond Earth. Into the Unknown.**

HORIZON 89 is an interactive lunar exploration platform designed to make space science, lunar missions, and Solar System exploration accessible through an immersive 3D experience.

The platform features an interactive 3D Solar System, Lunar Mission Control, historical lunar mission comparisons, coordinate-based study tools, and an AI-powered Mission Copilot.

Users can explore lunar missions such as IM-1 Odysseus, Blue Ghost Mission 1, and Peregrine Mission One, while learning about the Moon's south-polar region and available scientific information.

Built using React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Node.js, HORIZON 89 combines visualization, mission research, and AI-assisted exploration.

Our guiding principle is simple: **Every scientific claim should have a source.** The platform distinguishes verified information, schematic visualizations, and unavailable data to encourage transparent and responsible space exploration.

The project is currently demonstrated through GitHub Codespaces, with permanent hosting planned at **https://horizon89.earth**.
details:
HORIZON 89 – Beyond Earth. Into the Unknown.

Project Website: https://horizon89.earth

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/AB-Aayush-Sri-Nandan/horizon-89

HORIZON 89 is an interactive lunar exploration and mission intelligence platform designed to make lunar science, planetary exploration, and space mission research accessible through an immersive 3D digital environment.

The project combines interactive Solar System visualization, lunar mission research, coordinate-based lunar exploration, scientific data availability tools, and an AI-powered Mission Copilot.

Central Principle: Every scientific claim needs a source.

1. Interactive Solar System Explorer

HORIZON 89 provides an immersive 3D Solar System experience featuring selectable celestial bodies, orbital guides, animated planetary movement, camera focusing, and interactive navigation.

Users can explore the Solar System and transition into the lunar exploration workspace. Planetary sizes, distances, and orbital paths are schematic representations rather than accurate scale models or live ephemeris simulations.

2. Lunar Mission Control

The Lunar Mission Control environment provides an interactive workspace dedicated to lunar exploration.

Features include:

  • Interactive Moon visualization.
  • Zoom, rotation, panning, and camera controls.
  • Latitude and longitude-based study location selection.
  • Lunar coordinate grid and target selection.
  • Dedicated lunar south-polar study shortcut at 89°S.
  • UTC date and time selection.
  • Timeline playback and time controls.
  • Mission information and scientific availability panels.

The default study coordinate of 89°S, 0°E is an analyst-selected location, not a confirmed mission landing site.

3. Lunar Mission Intelligence

The platform includes a historical lunar mission catalogue featuring:

  • IM-1 – Odysseus
  • Blue Ghost Mission 1
  • Peregrine Mission One

Users can examine mission information, payload details, historical events, references, and mission comparisons.

4. NASA/JPL Horizons Integration

HORIZON 89 includes a server-side integration designed to retrieve astronomical observer geometry using the NASA/JPL Horizons API.

Its intended functionality includes lunar observer location inputs, UTC-based observation time, Sun and Earth geometry queries, source attribution, calculation metadata, response caching, and validation.

Live JPL connectivity has not yet been verified in the deployment environment.

5. Scientific Data and Availability

The project includes a scientific workspace that communicates which information is available, unavailable, or awaiting validated data integration.

Its architecture supports importing and validating lunar terrain datasets, with future possibilities including elevation, slope, illumination, permanently shadowed region research, and lunar site comparison.

These advanced datasets and analyses are not currently enabled with validated real-world data.

6. AI-Powered Mission Copilot

The Mission Copilot is an AI-assisted conversational research interface using a server-side Groq API integration.

It is designed to:

  • Answer lunar exploration questions.
  • Explain mission information.
  • Compare selected missions.
  • Provide contextual scientific explanations.
  • Incorporate available references.
  • Communicate missing data and uncertainty.

AI-generated responses are supplementary explanations, not authoritative scientific evidence. Production functionality requires a correctly configured backend, API key, and provider connectivity.

7. Scientific Transparency

HORIZON 89 distinguishes historical information, schematic visualizations, calculated astronomical information, analyst-selected coordinates, verified datasets, and unavailable or unverified information.

Its objective is to make space exploration engaging without confusing illustrative representations with actual scientific measurements.

8. Technology Stack

Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Lucide React.

Backend: Node.js 24, native HTTP server, server-side API integration, Groq API for AI-assisted responses.

9. NASA Resources

NASA resources are incorporated through planetary visualization assets, mission information, and technical references, including NASA 3D Resources, NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services, and NASA/JPL Horizons.

The project does not imply NASA affiliation, endorsement, or official mission status.

10. Future Development

Future development aims to introduce validated lunar elevation datasets, south-polar illumination and shadow analysis, improved JPL connectivity, expanded mission catalogues, advanced scientific comparison tools, stronger AI research capabilities, and permanent production deployment.

Conclusion

HORIZON 89 brings together planetary visualization, lunar mission intelligence, coordinate-based exploration, scientific transparency, and AI-assisted research.

It aims to create an accessible digital environment where students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts can explore the Moon, understand lunar missions, and discover the possibilities of future space exploration.

Project Website: https://horizon89.earth

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/AB-Aayush-Sri-Nandan/horizon-89
